NKJV.1: Cast your bread upon the waters,  For you will find it after many days.
NKJV.2: Give a serving to seven, and also to eight,  For you do not know what evil will be on the earth.
NKJV.3: If the clouds are full of rain, They empty themselves upon the earth; And if a tree falls to the south or the north, In the place where the tree falls, there it shall lie.
NKJV.4: He who observes the wind will not sow, And he who regards the clouds will not reap.
NKJV.5: As you do not know what is the way of the wind, Or how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child, So you do not know the works of God who makes everything.
NKJV.6: In the morning sow your seed, And in the evening do not withhold your hand; For you do not know which will prosper, Either this or that, Or whether both alike will be good.
NKJV.7: Truly the light is sweet, And it is pleasant for the eyes to behold the sun;
NKJV.8: But if a man lives many years And rejoices in them all, Yet let him remember the days of darkness, For they will be many. All that is coming is vanity.
NKJV.9: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth, And let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth;  Walk in the ways of your heart, And in the sight of your eyes; But know that for all these  God will bring you into judgment.
NKJV.10: Therefore remove sorrow from your heart, And put away evil from your flesh, For childhood and youth are vanity.

ESV.1: Cast your bread upon the waters, for you will find it after many days.
ESV.2: Give a portion to seven, or even to eight, for you know not what disaster may happen on earth.
ESV.3: If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth, and if a tree falls to the south or to the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it will lie.
ESV.4: He who observes the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will not reap.
ESV.5: As you do not know the way the spirit comes to the bones in the womb  of a woman with child, so you do not know the work of God who makes everything.
ESV.6: In the morning sow your seed, and at evening withhold not your hand, for you do not know which will prosper, this or that, or whether both alike will be good.
ESV.7: Light is sweet, and it is pleasant for the eyes to see the sun.
ESV.8: So if a person lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember that the days of darkness will be many. All that comes is vanity.
ESV.9: Rejoice, O young man, in your youth, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth. Walk in the ways of your heart and the sight of your eyes. But know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
ESV.10: Remove vexation from your heart, and put away pain  from your body, for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.

NASB.1: Cast your bread on the surface of the waters, for you will find it after many days.
NASB.2: Divide your portion to seven, or even to eight, for you do not know what misfortune may occur on the earth.
NASB.3: If the clouds are full, they pour out rain upon the earth; and whether a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, wherever the tree falls, there it lies.
NASB.4: He who watches the wind will not sow and he who looks at the clouds will not reap.
NASB.5: Just as you do not know the path of the wind and how bones [are formed] in the womb of the pregnant woman, so you do not know the activity of God who makes all things.
NASB.6: Sow your seed in the morning and do not be idle in the evening, for you do not know whether morning or evening sowing will succeed, or whether both of them alike will be good.
NASB.7: The light is pleasant, and [it is] good for the eyes to see the sun.
NASB.8: Indeed, if a man should live many years, let him rejoice in them all, and let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything that is to come [will be] futility.
NASB.9: Rejoice, young man, during your childhood, and let your heart be pleasant during the days of young manhood. And follow the impulses of your heart and the desires of your eyes. Yet know that God will bring you to judgment for all these things.
NASB.10: So, remove grief and anger from your heart and put away pain from your body, because childhood and the prime of life are fleeting.

AMP.1: Cast your bread on the surface of the waters, [be diligently active, make thoughtful decisions], for you will find it after many days.
AMP.2: Give a portion to seven, or even [divide it] to eight, for you do not know what misfortune may occur on the earth.
AMP.3: If the clouds are full [of rain], they empty themselves on the earth; and if a tree falls toward the south or toward the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it lies.
AMP.4: He who watches the wind [waiting for all conditions to be perfect] will not sow [seed], and he who looks at the clouds will not reap [a harvest].
AMP.5: Just as you do not know the way and path of the wind or how the bones are formed in the womb of a pregnant woman, even so you do not know the activity of God who makes all things.
AMP.6: Sow your seed in the morning and do not be idle with your hands in the evening, for you do not know whether morning or evening planting will succeed, whether this or that, or whether both alike will be good.
AMP.7: The light is sweet and pleasant, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.
AMP.8: Yes, if a man should live many years, let him rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. All that is to come will be futility.
AMP.9: Rejoice, young man, in your childhood, and let your heart be pleasant in the days of your young manhood. And walk in the ways of your heart and in the desires of your eyes, but know that God will bring you into judgment for all these things.
AMP.10: Therefore, remove sorrow and anger from your heart and put away pain from your body, for childhood and the prime of life are fleeting.

NLT.1:
Send your grain across the seas,
and in time, profits will flow back to you.
NLT.2:
But divide your investments among many places,
for you do not know what risks might lie ahead.
NLT.3:
When clouds are heavy, the rains come down.
Whether a tree falls north or south, it stays where it falls.
NLT.4:
Farmers who wait for perfect weather never plant.
If they watch every cloud, they never harvest.
NLT.5: Just as you cannot understand the path of the wind or the mystery of a tiny baby growing in its mother’s womb, so you cannot understand the activity of God, who does all things.
NLT.6: Plant your seed in the morning and keep busy all afternoon, for you don’t know if profit will come from one activity or another — or maybe both.
NLT.7: Light is sweet; how pleasant to see a new day dawning.
NLT.8: When people live to be very old, let them rejoice in every day of life. But let them also remember there will be many dark days. Everything still to come is meaningless.
NLT.9: Young people, it’s wonderful to be young! Enjoy every minute of it. Do everything you want to do; take it all in. But remember that you must give an account to God for everything you do.
NLT.10: So refuse to worry, and keep your body healthy. But remember that youth, with a whole life before you, is meaningless.

MSG.1:
Be generous: Invest in acts of charity.
Charity yields high returns.
MSG.2:
Don't hoard your goods; spread them around.
Be a blessing to others. This could be your last night.
MSG.3:
When the clouds are full of water, it rains.
When the wind blows down a tree, it lies where it falls.
MSG.4:
Don't sit there watching the wind. Do your own work.
Don't stare at the clouds. Get on with your life.
MSG.5:
Just as you'll never understand
the mystery of life forming in a pregnant woman,
So you'll never understand
the mystery at work in all that God does.
MSG.6:
Go to work in the morning
and stick to it until evening without watching the clock.
You never know from moment to moment
how your work will turn out in the end.
MSG.7:
Oh, how sweet the light of day,
And how wonderful to live in the sunshine!
MSG.8:
Even if you live a long time, don't take a single day for granted.
Take delight in each light-filled hour,
Remembering that there will also be many dark days
And that most of what comes your way is smoke.
MSG.9:
You who are young, make the most of your youth.
Relish your youthful vigor.
Follow the impulses of your heart.
If something looks good to you, pursue it.
But know also that not just anything goes;
You have to answer to God for every last bit of it.
MSG.10:
Live footloose and fancy free—
You won't be young forever.
Youth lasts about as long as smoke.

NIV.1:
Bread Upon the Waters
Cast your bread upon the waters,
for after many days you will find it again.
NIV.2:
Give portions to seven, yes to eight,
for you do not know what disaster may come upon the land.
NIV.3:
If clouds are full of water,
they pour rain upon the earth.
Whether a tree falls to the south or to the north,
in the place where it falls, there will it lie.
NIV.4:
Whoever watches the wind will not plant;
whoever looks at the clouds will not reap.
NIV.5:
As you do not know the path of the wind,
or how the body is formed in a mother’s womb,
so you cannot understand the work of God,
the Maker of all things.
NIV.6:
Sow your seed in the morning,
and at evening let not your hands be idle,
for you do not know which will succeed,
whether this or that,
or whether both will do equally well.
NIV.7:
Remember Your Creator While Young
Light is sweet,
and it pleases the eyes to see the sun.
NIV.8:
However many years a man may live,
let him enjoy them all.
But let him remember the days of darkness,
for they will be many.
Everything to come is meaningless.
NIV.9:
Be happy, young man, while you are young,
and let your heart give you joy in the days of your youth.
Follow the ways of your heart
and whatever your eyes see,
but know that for all these things
God will bring you to judgment.
NIV.10:
So then, banish anxiety from your heart
and cast off the troubles of your body,
for youth and vigor are meaningless.

NET.1: Send your grain overseas, for after many days you will get a return.
NET.2: Divide your merchandise among seven or even eight investments, for you do not know what calamity may happen on earth.
NET.3: If the clouds are full of rain, they will empty themselves on the earth, and whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, the tree will lie wherever it falls.
NET.4: He who watches the wind will not sow, and he who observes the clouds will not reap.
NET.5: Just as you do not know the path of the wind, or how the bones form in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you do not know the work of God who makes everything.
NET.6: Sow your seed in the morning, and do not stop working until the evening; for you do not know which activity will succeed — whether this one or that one, or whether both will prosper equally.
NET.7: Light is sweet, and it is pleasant for a person to see the sun.
NET.8: So, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all, but let him remember that the days of darkness will be many — all that is about to come is obscure.
NET.9: Rejoice, young man, while you are young, and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth. Follow the impulses of your heart and the desires of your eyes, but know that God will judge your motives and actions.
NET.10: Banish emotional stress from your mind. and put away pain from your body; for youth and the prime of life are fleeting.
